account:
Today repeated rumours suggest a bridge or port change is being discussed at the bakery without a clear public announcement. Townsfolk 21 named the baker, innkeeper, builder, freight, and neighbour as people present in various accounts. These are secondhand reports, not proof of a plan or of anyone's intentions. The neighbour also asked me for details and confirmed our three o'clock tea, so may simply be hearing the same rumours. I tried asking the baker directly, but the baker left before hearing my question. I suspect the talk concerns transport or river-crossing arrangements, but I do not know what change is proposed or why.

The scheduled ten o'clock mill grain inspection was poorly arranged: no miller appeared, and the secretary had neither a confirmed contact nor a grain location. The stall contained 68 hay bales priced at two emeralds each, as well as emeralds; I removed nothing. I asked the secretary to record the inspection as incomplete, find a responsible contact, and arrange follow-up. This could be ordinary disorganisation; I have no evidence connecting it to the rumours.

The treasury earlier held 128 emeralds and no accounts or correspondence. That alone does not establish missing money or misconduct. The builder reportedly says the hall lanterns are in good order, and an additional lighting inspection is booked for eighteen hundred. I have kept my noon home appointment and am now back at the office at thirteen hundred for council letters, with the secretary waiting nearby. I want to establish firsthand facts rather than turn the bakery rumours into accusations.
